programs.title: New Zealand by Train
programs.desc:
There are three railway routes in New Zealand.The first, Northern Explorer, stretches across the North Island, from Auckland to Wellington.Coastal Pacific runs from Picton to Christchurch, offering breathtaking views from the east coast of the South Island.The "TranzAlpine" route leads from Christchurch to the wild west coast.The total length of railway lines is 4,000 km.Their construction was extremely demanding and difficult.New Zealand, being a small island country, is characterized by a huge variety of terrain.Here you can find subtropical and rainforests, mountains, oceans, volcanoes and plains with railway tracks running through them.Each episode will discuss the engineering difficulties encountered during the construction of the railway network and present places worth seeing.Local residents talk about the everyday challenges that life in this area poses for them
The director of the "Lord of the Rings" trilogy, Peter Jackson, chose New Zealand as the setting for the adventures of the hobbit and his company.It is famous for its picturesque landscapes that are the perfect background for fantastic, out-of-this-world stories.They are extremely diverse - peaceful river valleys and green hills contrast with numerous volcanoes.However, such terrain constitutes a huge challenge for the engineers responsible for the construction of the railway.Viewers will learn about the attractions of the Kiwi country from the perspective of train passengers following three routes - Northern Explorer, Coastal Pacific and TranzAlpine.The Hobbit's Land The journey is divided into two stages.The first one goes through the North Island, where the capital Wellington and Auckland - the country's largest city - are located.There is no shortage of untouched areas that viewers of "The Lord of the Rings" could see.For example, the Ngauruhoe volcano located here played the role of Mount Doom.The Northern Explorer route is 681 km long.It runs via numerous viaducts from Auckland to Wellington.Passengers travel through, among others:farmland, the engineering masterpiece of the Raurimu Spiral and the volcanic plateau.The creators of the documentary combine phenomenal landscapes with a story about the culture and history of the end of the world.

programs.title: Exploration Volcano
programs.desc: Chris Horsley specializes in volcano exploration.In the program, he brings documentarians from around the world to volcanic trails to show them the effects of eruptions, which can wreak havoc and threaten communities.Chris's great expedition spans a wide range - from the jungles of the Congo to the lava-burnt cities of the Canary Islands, from the distinctive glacial plains of Iceland to the smoking archipelagos of Italy.In each episode, his team must face unique and unpredictable terrain.However, the team does not stop at anything.He wants to complete each mission, whether it's collecting molten lava straight from the source or installing state-of-the-art volcano monitoring systems.These activities are necessary to better understand the functioning of ruthless natural giants.

programs.title: Spy in the Ocean
programs.desc:
The creators of the four-episode series present the journey of specially constructed animal replicas equipped with cameras to the ocean.Their goal is to bring closer the deeply hidden life of creatures inhabiting this inaccessible and dynamic ecosystem.Using breakthrough technology, including:modern LCD screens, record surprising behaviors and relationships of sea animals.Viewers will see colorful coral reefs, rocky coastlines, Thai macaques fishing, unusual behavior of seals, socialization of sperm whales and a complicated ritual between hermit crabs.The over thirty spies include a sperm whale, a herring, a puffer, a hermit crab, a clownfish and a dolphin.The production took three years on four oceans of the world
Filmmakers used new technologies to present the magic of the underwater world from a previously unavailable perspective.Robots equipped with cameras - confusingly similar to sea animals - set off on a spy mission.They not only passively recorded their surroundings, but also interacted with representatives of various species.The spectacular recordings were made into a documentary series that combines a fascinating narrative with impressive photos and humor.Its characters include sperm whales, octopuses, macaques, puffers, crabs and marlins.Underwater Geniuses One of the robotic spies took the form of a baby sperm whale.Not only cameras were installed there, but also hydrophones recording sounds.The three-meter-long baby was supposed to arouse the maternal instinct of the female it encountered.It greeted him with characteristic clicks.The moving meeting scene gave insight into the social intelligence of these giants.On an isolated Thai island, a dummy monkey spied on a diving flock of macaques.Cameras recorded their clever use of tools and carefree fun.In turn, the mechanical cephalopod went to meet the coconut octopus.Their interaction showed that true geniuses live in depths inaccessible to man.
